description_full: Lamar Advertising Company is one of the largest outdoor advertising companies in North America, with over 362,000 displays across the United States and Canada. Lamar offers advertisers a variety of billboards, interstate logo, transit and airport advertising formats, helping both local businesses and national brands reach broad audiences every day. In addition to its more traditional out-of-home inventory, Lamar is proud to offer its customers the largest network of digital billboards in the United States with over 5,400 displays. Lamar Advertising Company was founded and incorporated in 1902 in Delaware and is based in Baton Rouge, United States.
ceo_bio: Mr. Sean E. Reilly J.D. | CEO & President | Age 63 | Compensation: $2.6M (FY2025)

Stock-based compensation of $10K per employee reflects an ownership culture. CEO compensation is 4× revenue per employee (modest relative to workforce productivity). Governance score flags moderate compensation governance risk (4/10).
financial_summary: Lamar Advertising Company is a large-cap real estate business with a $15.8B market cap on $2.3B of annual revenue.
The top line has compounded at +4% over the past three years, which puts it in mature, slow-growth territory.
Returns on capital run at 13% against a 9% cost of capital, a 4-point spread that creates value, though narrow enough that competitive pressure could close it.

The business throws off $683M in free cash flow — roughly 30 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, and cash conversion sits at 1.47× so those profits are backed by real cash.
On the balance sheet, debt is moderate at 3.0× net debt/EBITDA, serviceable in normal conditions but worth watching through a downturn, and interest coverage runs at 4.8×.

Shareholder yield of 4.5% reflects a genuine commitment to returning capital rather than empire-building, and insider ownership is negligible, so management has little personal stake in the long-term outcome, and within its sector the business captures 1.7× its fair share of profits, a structural advantage visible in the numbers.
